memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not pervert justice; do not show partiality to the poor or favouritism to the great, but judge your neighbour fairly.'" - Lev 19:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read that carefully, because it cuts in a direction we might not expect. Do not show partiality to the poor.

We understand the second half instantly — do not favour the rich and powerful. That corruption is familiar everywhere. But God also forbids tilting a verdict towards the poor out of sympathy.

Why? Because justice that bends in any direction stops being justice. If a court favours the poor as a matter of course, then truth no longer decides cases — category does. And a system like that eventually harms everyone, including the poor.

God cares intensely for the poor. This chapter has already proved that with the gleaning laws. But caring for the poor is not the same as distorting the truth about a particular case.

That distinction is worth holding. We can be generous in mercy and rigorous about facts. In fact we must be. Justice, justice you shall pursue, says Deuteronomy (16:20).

It applies in ordinary life too. When you hear a dispute between two people, do you weigh what actually happened? Or do you decide based on who you like better, who is more like you, who tells the better story?

Judge your neighbour fairly. Both neighbours.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you form judgements based on evidence or on who you prefer?
2. Where have you let sympathy or dislike distort your assessment?
3. How can you be both merciful and truthful at the same time?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are perfectly just and perfectly merciful. Teach me to weigh things fairly, without favouring the powerful or bending truth out of sympathy. Amen.
